clue.text: Frame for little prince and princess?

blocks.note: Chas is the short form of Charles, the name of the Prince of Wales
a short pet form for a girl, read as a little princess: Sisi was the nickname of an Austrian empress

explanation.surface: A cot or carriage frame built for two royal children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little' works on both names: the prince and the princess each appear in clipped, pet-name form.
explanation.definitionFit: A chassis is the supporting structure of a car or machine, the base onto which everything else is fitted.

clue.text: A speaker in church - more likely in mosque

indicators.note: something placed in a building sits inside it, so the first pieces go inside the church abbreviation

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for church
taken as written
the lip shapes speech; lip also means cheeky talk

explanation.surface: A preacher in a church, set against the leader you would more likely hear in a mosque.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: an Islamic ruler belongs in a mosque rather than a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A caliph was the religious and civil head of the Muslim world, a figure associated with Islam rather than Christian worship.

clue.text: Prince with watching brief starting within

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that letter is kept
within tells us that one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: someone watching carefully is alert
the opening letter of brief

explanation.surface: A prince sits in court holding a watching brief for some interested party.
explanation.walkthrough: A watching brief is a lawyer's brief to observe a case; here the words are split into a synonym and a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Albert was Queen Victoria's consort, the most famous royal of that name.

clue.text: Fur-clad listener at church within reach of engine?

indicators.note: something clad in fur is wrapped up in it, so the fur goes around the following pieces

blocks.note: sable is a costly dark fur
the ear is what listens
standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A worshipper in a fur coat listens in church, near a steam engine of some sort.
explanation.walkthrough: The engine is a search engine: anything it can reach online can be found.
explanation.definitionFit: Data that a search engine can find and index is described as searchable, the punning sense of the question.

clue.text: Survey ends with large number (minus 21) at 19 (qv)

indicators.note: ends asks for the outer letters of the word in front of it
minus means take away, so the answer to another clue is removed from the big number

blocks.note: the first and last letters of survey
a billion is a very large number
the answer to 21 across

explanation.surface: A survey reveals a huge sum, less a big cat, at a hotel to be looked up elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 is TOWERS: Sybil Fawlty runs Fawlty Towers, played by Prunella Scales, the puzzle's birthday girl. BILLION minus LION leaves BIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Sybil is the hotelier's wife at Fawlty Towers in the BBC sitcom, so she is the person found at that hotel.

clue.text: Pet with the arms folded

indicators.note: folded things are bent and rearranged, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pet animal sitting with its little arms crossed.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamster is a small burrowing rodent commonly kept as a children's pet in a cage.

clue.text: Caricatured in Punch with first cigarette, not breathing properly

indicators.note: a caricature distorts its subject, so these letters are distorted into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
first is one, the Roman numeral I
cig is the everyday short form of cigarette

explanation.surface: A smoker, sketched in the comic magazine Punch, lights a first cigarette and wheezes.
explanation.walkthrough: Punch was a long-running British humour magazine famous for cartoons, which is why caricature seems to belong to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiccuping is a spasm of the diaphragm that interrupts normal breathing with sudden involuntary gulps.

clue.text: Chart on page associated with Caribbean saint by Benson

definitions.text: associated with Caribbean saint by Benson

blocks.note: a map is a chart
standard abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: A map drawn on a page, connected with a West Indian island by some writer named Benson.
explanation.walkthrough: E. F. Benson wrote the Mapp and Lucia novels; St Lucia is the Caribbean island. Prunella Scales played Mapp on TV.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss Mapp is paired with Lucia in Benson's comic novels, so she is the character linked to that saint's name.

clue.text: Figures with some parallels - gin sounds less trouble!

indicators.note: sounds tells us to go by what is heard when the words are spoken

blocks.note: a gin is a snare for animals
something less troublesome is easier; said in a British accent the final r is dropped

explanation.surface: A drinker finds gin makes life feel easier.
explanation.walkthrough: Gin here is the snare, not the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Trapezia are four-sided figures with one pair of parallel sides, so they have some, but not all, sides parallel.

clue.text: Drink from river - that's one with gin

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for river
ie, id est, means that is
a gin sling is a classic cocktail

explanation.surface: Someone drinks from a river and is offered gin to go with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Riesling is a white wine made from the grape of the same name, chiefly in Germany and Alsace.

clue.text: Sign lots of books

indicators.note: lots of means a large part but not all, so the end of the word is dropped

blocks.note: a library is a collection of books

explanation.surface: Someone autographs a great pile of books.
explanation.walkthrough: Most of the word for a book collection is kept, losing its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Libra, the Scales, is the seventh sign of the zodiac; a nod to the theme's Prunella Scales.

clue.text: Mail behind taxi read the other way by Irish knight (deceased)

indicators.note: reading in the opposite direction turns the word around

blocks.note: a cab is a taxi
Knight of St Patrick, the old Irish order of chivalry
the late means dead

explanation.surface: Post trails a taxi, studied backwards by a dead Irish nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: Mail here is armour, and behind is the back of it; it looks like post following a taxi.
explanation.definitionFit: A backplate is the piece of plate armour that protects a knight's back, part of a suit of mail.

clue.text: Alchemist's friends keep people American

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: pals are friends
a race is a people
abbreviation for United States, hence American

explanation.surface: An alchemist's circle of friends harbours an American among them.
explanation.walkthrough: Add 12 and rearrange to get the preamble's PRUNELLA SCALES, whose birthday this was.
explanation.definitionFit: Paracelsus was the sixteenth-century Swiss physician and alchemist, a pioneer of chemical medicine.

clue.text: Heard sound at death of little heroine?

indicators.note: heard tells us the word is taken by its sound alone

blocks.note: a knell is the bell tolled for a death

explanation.surface: A bell is heard tolling as the little heroine dies.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Nell's death in Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop is famous; the K is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Nell is the child heroine of Dickens's novel The Old Curiosity Shop.

clue.text: Exactly as the fair fool gets round to performing

blocks.note: just means fair
an ass is a fool
round is the shape of the letter O
on stage, performing

explanation.surface: A fool at the fair goes into his act.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the front: the phrase means as readily or at the same moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Just as soon (as) means at exactly the same time as, matching the sense of exactly as.

clue.text: Blunt question, but curtailed amid continuous wear and tear

indicators.note: curtailed means its tail is cut, so the final letter goes
amid means in the middle of, so the short piece goes inside

blocks.note: the word but without its last letter
attrition is gradual wearing down

explanation.surface: A bluntly put question about steady wear and tear.
explanation.walkthrough: Blunt is Anthony Blunt, art historian and Surveyor of the Queen's Pictures, whose field was deciding who painted what.
explanation.definitionFit: Attribution of a painting to an artist is the central question in an art historian's work.

clue.text: This is defective and more or less completely obsolete

indicators.note: defective means lacking something, here the words that follow are what the first word lacks

blocks.note: the word This missing the letters i and s
roughly means approximately

explanation.surface: Something broken and pretty much entirely out of date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This is defective' means This with is taken out. THROUGHLY is the archaic form of thoroughly.
explanation.definitionFit: Throughly is an old word meaning thoroughly, which is to say completely, and now out of use.

clue.text: Drunk about half the wine at the top of the list before nightfall

indicators.note: half of a word means keeping only part of its letters, here the first part
the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter
about means surrounding, so the drunk word goes around the rest

blocks.note: tight is slang for drunk
the first two of the four letters of wine
the opening letter of list

explanation.surface: A drinker who has half-finished the wine list before evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Twilight is the dim light between sunset and full darkness, the time just before nightfall.

clue.text: Two fellows mistreated in La Dolce Vita?

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so the three letters before it are rearranged

blocks.note: he is a man and a don is a college fellow
the first syllable of this word is the fodder; the rest of it is the instruction

explanation.surface: Two men behaving badly in Fellini's film of Roman high living.
explanation.walkthrough: The word mistreated is split: its first syllable is the fodder and the rest is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedonism is the pursuit of pleasure, which the film title La Dolce Vita, the sweet life, exemplifies.

clue.text: Maker of revolver reported order on parade ground

indicators.note: reported means passed on by word of mouth, so we go by sound

blocks.note: a drill command telling a line of soldiers to turn

explanation.surface: A gunsmith's order shouted on a parade ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The revolver is not a gun but anything that turns round: a wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheelwright is a craftsman who makes wheels, and a wheel is a thing that revolves.

clue.text: People who draw structures that sound defective on TV

definitions.text: structures that sound defective on TV

blocks.note: those who tow or pull something along

blocks.clueFragment: structures that sound defective on TV
blocks.note: tall structures, in a TV title whose first word sounds like faulty

explanation.walkthrough: Fawlty Towers was the BBC sitcom in which Prunella Scales played Sybil; Fawlty sounds like faulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Towers are people who tow, and tall buildings, as in the hotel name of the sitcom.

clue.text: Now I'll get my ball back that's gone into net, won't I?

definitions.text: Now I'll get my ball back

indicators.note: the answer has gone into the following words and sits inside them

blocks.note: spanning the end of into, all of net and the start of won't

explanation.surface: A footballer passes, expecting a return, and asks whether the ball has gone in.
explanation.walkthrough: In football a one-two is a quick pass to a teammate who passes straight back.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-two is the move in which a player passes and immediately receives the ball back from a teammate.

clue.text: Joiner's part of the Dream - first of Cats?

blocks.note: in A Midsummer Night's Dream, Snug the joiner plays this role
the king of beasts, foremost of the big cats

explanation.walkthrough: 'first of Cats' looks like an instruction to take the letter C; it means the leading cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Snug the joiner plays the lion in the mechanicals' play, and the lion is called king of the cat family.

clue.text: Corked port once? Vicky etc won't worry

indicators.note: to worry something is to tug it about, so these letters are shaken into a new order

blocks.note: Queen Victoria and others of her kind
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sealed port bottle, and Victoria and friends who refuse to fret.
explanation.walkthrough: Queenstown was the name of Cobh, the port in County Cork, until 1920; Corked means in Cork. Prunella Scales played Queen Victoria.
explanation.definitionFit: Queenstown is the former name of the Irish port of Cobh in County Cork.

clue.text: Is this the feeling that corrupts the genuine heart?

definitions.text: Is this the feeling that corrupts the genuine heart?

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its inside, everything but the first and last letters
to corrupt something is to spoil its proper order

blocks.note: genuine without its outer letters

explanation.surface: Wondering whether boredom is what spoils sincere feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a fair description: boredom can sap real enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless weariness and boredom, a feeling that can drain sincere enthusiasm from a person.

clue.text: The Guardian way is golden

blocks.note: the editorial we, the newspaper speaking of itself
abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A boast that this newspaper's way of doing things is golden.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the golden West of the setting sun and the American frontier; it also names actor Timothy West, Prunella Scales's husband.
explanation.definitionFit: The West is traditionally called golden, after the sunset and the gold rush lands of the American frontier.

clue.text: Ladybird for money taking male name

blocks.note: a guinea was an old British coin worth 21 shillings
he is the male pronoun
abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A spotted beetle bought with cash, given a man's name.
explanation.walkthrough: Ladybird is split: a lady bird, a female fowl, not the spotted beetle.
explanation.definitionFit: A guinea hen is the female of the guinea fowl, so literally a female bird.

clue.text: Public transport from Dover to Calais

indicators.note: the letters are carried across from the place names that follow, lifted out of them

blocks.note: spanning most of Dover and the first letter of to
surface padding completing the cross-Channel route

explanation.surface: Public ferry services across the Channel from Dover to Calais.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means done openly and in public view, rather than hidden or secret.

clue.text: 24 - otherwise it's a moment at th' end of the play

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so the two letters are swapped round
the end of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: taken as written
a mo is a short moment
taken as written
the final letter of play

explanation.surface: A stage cue: at the play's end, a moment for an actor named in another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 is WEST; the answer completes the name of the actor Timothy West, Prunella Scales's husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Timothy is the first name of the actor Timothy West, so it goes with the answer to 24.

clue.text: As a producer of plays one needs one's company

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written without the apostrophe
standard abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A theatre producer needs a company of actors of their own.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugene Ionesco was the Romanian-French dramatist of the Theatre of the Absurd, who wrote plays like Rhinoceros.
